utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before we have the witness, there is some schedule matters I would like to announce. Tomorrow, we will have our sittings in Courtroom II at 2.15, and on Friday next week, because of the problem of scheduling, we will have no sitting on Friday next week. It is our intention to finish the testimony of the next witness today, at the request of the Defence counsel because of the protective measures. So as for the next witness, we would like to ask the Defence counsel to limit his direct examination to one hour, and we also give the same amount of time to the cross-examination so as to ensure that we will finish the next witness today. Having said that, Mr. Usher, could we have the witness, please? Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. Good afternoon. I will be very brief. While we are waiting for the witness, you must have read my thoughts when you said what you did. The Defence, and I have to say it for the record, Mr. Vinko Martinovic's Defence, Mr. Par and I, have never, not once, exceeded more than 50 per cent of the time of the Prosecution's direct examination. Neither yesterday, nor shall we in the future, exceed the time in our direct examination that we have announced. We were always very disciplined and we have always complied with the schedule and the timetable. We have witnesses here whom we planned to hear until the end of this week. So Mr. President, will you please warn the Prosecutor not to waste time? The witness is not to blame if he doesn't understand the question. The question is made understandable by the Prosecution. The Prosecutor says we've spent 20 minutes dealing with a matter. Now is this the witness's responsibility for the Prosecutor's? Let us have Prosecutors phrase the questions in a manner that will allow to use the time as best we can rather than waste it, and I hope that you will proceed, Mr. President, with the measures that you have announced at the beginning because it is the Prosecution which wastes time. The Defence has never exceeded the time allotted to it, either through the cross-examination or during the direct examination, and I object very seriously because the Prosecutor was allowed to do it yesterday, before -- earlier, and we are afraid he will also try to do that in the future. But that is not the responsibility of Defence and we do not have to cut anything short. After this witness, we shall have another witness who will be here today only. And whose direct examination will take less than 60 minutes. He has to leave tomorrow so I hope you will stand by your decision that the cross-examination should not exceed that time. As for this witness, Mr. Martinovic, even the Prosecutor alleges that his evidence is not of much value because he is the accused's brother. Then why doesn't he give up the cross-examination? However, the witness is under oath and I must say that ubi lex non distinguit, nec nos distinguere debemus, that is, where law doesn't distinguish, we should not make it either, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, first of all, I have to thank you for your cooperation about your direct examination. Secondly, since we have the witness here, we are not going to discuss about any detailed matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. We won't keep you long this afternoon, are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness nods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, before we continue on, I wanted to ask you about a similar name, name similar to one I asked you about yesterday and I want to make it clear I'm not suggesting that the other person, that there is confusion about the other person. I'm asking about another person but perhaps having a similar name. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, should the witness answer the question first?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'd be happy for him to Judge Clark, and I was just responding to counsel's objection but I'm happy to have the witness not review the document until he first gives an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness I would ask you not to review -- it's in English in any event. You perhaps read English but would you not look at that document for a moment, in light of the question raised by Judge Clark? I put to you a question and really we didn't get an answer. So can you please tell us if you were aware of any allegation or information about your brother running one or more "private prisons"?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did anyone from the international community ever approach you for information whether your brother was engaged in such activity?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me personally?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It continues to be your testimony, I take it, sir, since yesterday that at no time was your brother holding prisoners in a garage in West Mostar?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, of course I'm slightly jittery and a little bit tired after all this. Last night, when I returned to the hotel, and I suppose like any other witness who comes here, I turned the film back just trying to recapitulate to see how it went. Yesterday, you and I on two occasions, if I may put it in this way, talked at cross-purposes, say. One was about the year 1992, June, and the second one was your insistence on a garage. I still say today that there was no garage. However, you are right in one thing. Next to the building where Vinko's base, that is command, was, there was a workshop, a car mechanics, a car repair shop. Now, if you call a car shop a garage, perhaps it's funny to you, but it's not funny to me, because garage is used to park cars and a workshop is used to repair cars. There is a difference between the two in the workshop you will find the bay over which cars are driven and you do not find this thing in a garage. So I am sorry but that is how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I appreciate very much that clarification. Did it really not occur to you at any time yesterday that the questions I was asking you would include some place where cars were worked on and in fact didn't I ask you about whether any of the prisoners worked on vehicles for your brother's unit?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I also said that there were people who worked on cars, but you insisted on the word "garage." And I have a garage at home. Doors open, vehicles in, and that is all. So I'm sorry, again, but I suppose we simply did not understand one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So can we take it, can the Judges understand, then, sir, that in reference to all the questions yesterday about a garage being immediately adjacent to your brother's headquarters, if I change the term and say a workshop where cars were worked on, then all your answers would change from no to yes? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this question, Mr. President, namely to ask a question in such a laconic manner and expect such a laconic answer without repeating the substance of yesterday's questions, I think would mean setting the witness up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll move on and I submit for the record that the result is clear, that if the witness has already said that indeed there was a workshop where cars were worked on next to the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that you also just mentioned that there was some sort of a bay or a pit in that garage, for instance, where one would drive a car over and someone would work in such a pit? Under a car or a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, a garage that you mention, that is the workshop which includes a pit, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, in light of the questions or excuse me the answers of the witness, I will move on from 751 but nonetheless in response to counsel's questions, that is the basis for my putting the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us how you're currently employed?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Currently, I am involved in the construction in the town of Mostar, that is I'm building a residential house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you ever have a financial or other ownership interest in a company or business called Euroherc?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What kind of a business was that?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an insurance company.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where is -- any one in the family of a man named Ivica Licic also a co-owner or participant in that same business?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the family, one of the brothers of the gentleman you mentioned, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Which brother was that, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there unfortunately it's really not my habit to stand, to be on my feet all the time but I object to these questions. Why is that relevant? What is the relevance either to this case or challenging -- to challenge the credibility of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the Prosecutor is entitled to challenge the credibility of this witness. You may proceed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was the name of this brother of Ivica Lucic?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the brother Ivica Lucic, is this the same Ivica Lucic who was the head of one of the Bosnian Croat intelligence services?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, from the press, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And have you ever had any perhaps not Euroherc but any other financial or business dealings with Ivica Lucic, the former head of Bosnian Croat intelligence?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never met that gentleman in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was Mr. Bruno Stojic or his family also a co-owner or a participant in the Euroherc business, the former Minister of Defence of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And have you had any other business interest with Mr. Stojic other than Euroherc?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that I had any business interests with Mr. Bruno Stojic. In other words, Mr. Bruno Stojic did not have any interest in the Euroherc company.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, when I asked you a moment ago, and perhaps you may be rights, perhaps it was someone in his family but when I asked you this question and I'll simply read it to you again: Was Mr. Bruno Stojic or his family also a co-owner or participant in it should say Euroherc business and your answer at line 9 was yes. So in what way, sir, did you indicate yes?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You -- there were two questions in one. When I said yes, I meant somebody -- a member of his family. So you want me to repeat, yes, a member of his family, his eldest brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what is his name, please?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mate, if -- but I stand to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you've talked on a number of occasions about essentially a conspiracy against your brother or efforts to blame him or sacrifice him, I believe you've said. Have you ever heard that a man -- two men that named Marko Radic and Ivan Hrkac, as two men that your brother has blamed for charges being brought against him?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To avoid once again a similar situation as a moments before because you asked me two questions in one, I've heard of these two persons but whether Vinko is accusing them of something, I do not know. So, yes, I've heard of Marko Radic, no, I even know him personally. I believe we were school fellows. I've heard Ivan Hrkac's name but I've never seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you ever know your brother to assert that it was partly Mr. Naletilic's, Tuta's, fault that he had been charged?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. If I could direct your attention, sir, with the usher's assistance to Exhibit P851.02?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, I would like to know the Defence would like to know the source of this document. That is the first thing. Where did this document come from? I see what it says here but that is impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, if you could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll be happy to have discussions about the authenticity its of a document outside the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will deal with this issue when we are admitting the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'll just read one --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if a document is given to the witness, then to be fair, the Defence needs to know the source of this document. If we want to exclude the witness, why don't we send him out for a while? But this is also something new. We have never before sent a witness out of the room while we were discussing an exhibit, but one cannot ask this witness a question if we don't know the source. This is a handwritten document, so many things are crossed over on it, we don't know the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not just the source but also the legality, the way the document has been obtained, if we can consider this a document or exhibit at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik and Mr. Seric, as for this document, I believe, in the -- in the bundle of documents the Prosecutor has indicated the source of that document. And during the cross-examination, the Prosecution could ask questions about this document, and the witness has the full right to confirm or deny anything in this document, and when we are admitting this document into the evidence, we will look into the source, the authenticity of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the source is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assert, Your Honours, that the source is not correct. The Prosecutor knows it. And he still writes that the source is Vinko Martinovic. This is not correct. This is simply not correct, from the very beginning. If something is founded on the wrong foundations, we cannot proceed. We cannot move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm not going to any longer debate. Well, Witness, could I ask you to leave this room for a little while? We are discuss a document which has nothing to do with you. It's a legal issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott? With the absence of the witness, you may shed some light on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The source of this document is that it was when Mr. Martinovic came into the custody of this Tribunal, he had a brief case with him which was taken and the material there in collected and inventoried by the Registrar. And at that time, the Registrar gave to the Office of the Prosecutor the contents of that brief case, after having inventoried it. And that's where this document comes from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is that a satisfactory answer? Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am astonished. I can't tell you whether I'm satisfied or not satisfied with this answer. Does this mean stolen or later on inserted in the file? What is this all about? I'm really deeply shocked. This is not an explanation of the source. The document is then stolen, if this explanation is correct. A file has been taken away from somebody and something was found inside. Is there any confirmation of that? Was Mr. Martinovic aware that his room was searched, that the documents were taken, from the very first day, this gentleman has been exposed to -- I don't dare say what. This is illegal treatment of my client, from the very first day. This is a shame, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to share the astonishment and I would like to -- the person from the registry to be examined. If this is true, we cannot use the document until we examine the authenticity of this allegation by the Prosecution. For the registry to engage in such dealings together with the Prosecutor is really shameful and this is an understatement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Gentlemen, can I just say something for a moment? We are not talking about the contents of the document. We are talking about how the document came to be in the hands of the Prosecution, and let's concentrate on that aspect of the case. I think the Judges really want to consult about this for a little while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, do you have anything to add about the source of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not really. We could call -- I mean -- we could call a representative of the Registrar if that becomes necessary but I've told the Chamber as directly as I could, whether asked, what the source of the document was, and that's my information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if this is the case, I'm afraid that after consultation among the Judges, this document should not be used in this courtroom until you have further information about the source of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. Thank you for your ruling, but I must say that it says here that this is a new document. We should have received it at the same time the Prosecutor received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if this document will not be tendered or admitted into the evidence, we will return this document to the Registrar. Could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I'm sorry for you to have to wait for so long. Would you please sit down and we will continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott. You may move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, just to follow up on the last question before moving on, just so the record is clear in light of the some of the intervention that were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. made, did you ever have any conversation with your brother about any role that allegedly Mr. Naletilic may have played in him being charged?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe the role is different between the Defence counsel and the Prosecutor but when I asked similar questions, and when my learned friend objected, you asked me to skip the question and I would skip it. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not going into any document. I'm simply clarifying the last answer put by the witness before all this happened and it's a question he can answer either yes or no he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really do not remember the question, Your Honours. Can the Prosecutor please repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever have any conversation with your brother about any role that allegedly Mr. Naletilic may have played in your brother being charged?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever know, during the war in 1993, a man named Predrag Mandic?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you know a man named Mario Milicevic?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there are two men with the same name but I believe that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, did you know a Mario Milicevic that was the head of another unit that was referred to as an ATG?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mario Milicevic lives in my neighbourhood in which I used to live and in which Vinko used to live. That's where I know him. I know who you're talking about. I know the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was he the commander of something called the Vinko Penavic ATG?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's been pointed out to me, Mr. President, just so there is no confusion it's been translated Vinko probably perhaps I misspoke. It should be Benko Penavic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, a little while ago, we heard the Prosecutor asking the witness to list the names of the co-owners or the families of the co-owners of the company that the witness owned. This has led us no where. Now, again, he is asking the witness to list the names which were not mentioned on direct, and I'm afraid this, again, is not going to lead anywhere. This is just a waste of time, I'm afraid. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's hope for the best, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, was he the commander of the Benko Penavic unit?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to say something before I answer your question. Whether you call it Vinko or Benko or whether you believe it or not, believe me this doesn't mean a thing to me. These first names, these last names were in such an abundance and they were mentioned so often, and I never took any interest in those names. If you say Benko Penavic, let me answer be yes, but it really doesn't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think you said yesterday, sir, that you considered that at least this man that you've mentioned Ernest Takac may have considered himself a deputy of your brother's unit or did you believe he was a deputy of your brother's unit?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I said that. I wish somebody could read to me what I said, because I don't think that is what I said, and I can really not repeat exactly what I said, and I asked you yesterday not to ask from me to repeat literally what I said. You are asking me a lot of questions. You are trying to confuse me. You have these things on paper. I have nothing on paper. And I can really not repeat exactly what I said yesterday. In any event, the way you put it to me, I am certain that that is not what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, I'm not going to ask to you use the exact words that you've used previously but just then if that's the case, tell us again in your own or different words what role did you understand, if any, did Mr. Takac play in the Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, when you asked me, I believe you asked me who Vinko Martinovic's deputies were in his unit, and I believe that I said the following, that it could have been somebody called Peric, somebody whose last name was Jakovljevic and I don't know what else I said. When you asked me about Takac, Takac was half savage, somebody who was not easily commanded and I assume that he could not have been a commander. I believe he would have been only too happy to be a commander but he could not be a commander because he was too rowdy, too wild.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I believe you said he was disobedient. My question is disobedient to who?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I said that he was disobedient, I suppose that he was disobedient to somebody who issued him orders, and if somebody is a wild, rowdy and savage, then he doesn't obey anybody. If you want to ask me whether he was disobedient to Vinko, then I assume he was also disobedient to Vinko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you said that at some point your brother, Mr. Takac had some falling out in so many words and your brother essentially said good riddance to him. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you will find that in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So your brother and Mr. Takac did not have a falling out then and they remained together throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that, but a little while ago you said something that I haven't said so far, and I also didn't say that they stayed together. Please ask me specific questions and believe me, I shall answer them, if I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did a time ever come when the relationship between your brother and Mr. Takac changed?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What do you say happened?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What exactly happened, I don't know but I know that Takac with a few other men left the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately when that was, sir?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could ask the witness to be shown Exhibit 634? Sir, this is a document that's previously been admitted into evidence, of a statement from the man Ernest Takac, and in fact, you will see, if you have a chance to look at it, it relates to the same event that the statement that we looked at yesterday with your brother, which is Exhibit 633, and according to both Mr. Takac's statement, Exhibit P634 and your brother's statement, P633, can you not agree with me, sir, that at least as of October, 1993, your brother and Mr. Takac were still working quite closely together?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the dates are identical on both documents, on the one you showed me yesterday and the one you're showing me today, then this should be correct. And as to how close they were, I can't tell you that just looking at these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that your brother and Mr. Takac continued to be members of the same units even after they both left the Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me? I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that contrary to the fact -- contrary to having any sort of falling out, at least in 1993, your brother Stela and Mr. Takac continued to be members of the same units, HVO units, together, even after the Vinko Skrobo unit, correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Vinko Skrobo is a unit, Vinko's unit, with which he was on the Bulevar, by the health centre and which -- with which he was fighting against Muslims, after that unit, as far as I know, Vinko was no longer a soldier of any other unit. I may allow that I don't know, but I would say that he was not a member of any other unit after that unit, and as for Takac, I really wouldn't be able to tell you whether he was a member of any other unit or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibits 819 and 818?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Directing your attention first of all to 819, do you recall, sir --

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- That your brother, Stela, Vinko Martinovic, Mr. Pehar, Mr. Takac were indicated to have continued for sometime, for approximately a four month period to be members of something called the ATJ Domovina? From June to October, 1994?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of the existence of the ATJ Domovina, the first time ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of something called the 22nd Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are already very far when you're talking about 22nd, 27th Sabotage. This is not my turf. I can say no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you look at Exhibit 818? Doesn't that indicate that again your brother, Mr. Pehar, Mr. Takac continued together to be members of that unit even into 1995?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not dispute that these names are indeed here. But once again, I repeat -- can I please have the other one, Mr. Usher? I have two documents in front of me, and the same five names on both of them, and on one it says ATJ Domovina and on the other, the 22nd Sabotage Detachment. That seems to be a lot of armies, too many armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell the Judges, please, have either your father, Ivan Martinovic or yourself, sir, ever been involved in contacting either witnesses for the Prosecution or witnesses to assist your brother?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you describe those activities to us, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the question was setting up the witness and we heard the positive answer. Can, please, the Prosecutor split the question in order not to confuse the witness? Can he be precise and tell exactly which witnesses he is referring to in his question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that's very difficult for the Prosecution to do so. I think, you know, the witness heard your objection, and he will give us an explanation about that. Yes, Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am here in The Hague with four other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can we go to private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, due or your father know a man named Mustafa Sukelic?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And have you ever approached Mr. Sukelic about being a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Has your father, to your knowledge, ever approached Mr. Sukelic about either being or not being a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, and that was your question, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I'll ask you my final two questions, similar questions, about this man that you've mentioned in your testimony already, Halil Ajanic. Have you or your father ever contacted Mr. Ajanic about either being or not being a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And have you or your father ever moved about Mostar looking and asking people, trying to find Mr. Ajanic?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, any re-examination, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only two, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please give the witness Exhibit 633 and 18 -- and 818? Excuse me, in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at the first -- at the Croatian version of 633? Croatian version. And look at the signature. You said that it was very similar and that you granted that it could be your brother's signature. Now, look at Exhibit 818, and tell us if it is your brother's signature in both these documents? Under one, of course.

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose everybody can see no, that it is far from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Say yes or no, let us finish that?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I said about there one that it is possible, about this I think that it is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from Judges? Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Martinovic, I just have one question for you and I know you've been here an exceptionally long time so I won't hold you. I may not have it in front of you but the map that you had, P11.018, yes, very good, I just want to ask you a question on that map. No, it doesn't need to be in private session but I just want to you look at the map. You don't have to put it on the ELMO. Obviously, I'm not good at maps. If I were I probably wouldn't need to ask this question. But you told us, I think it was yesterday, that on the morning of the 9th of May, you and a companion were driving from, the transcript said Ahmici but I doubt that that's correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely incorrect. I could not have said that. Absolutely wrong. I am sorry, I must have said all sorts of things during these past two days but that is one thing that I'm sure I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I didn't think. It was probably something that sounded like it but on the map you said it was the direction you came from was the west side of Mostar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: What would be -- looking at the map, you don't need to put it on the ELMO, do you see that there are a number of towns marked as directions, like Rastani over to the north and Citluk and Medjugorje to the south, and the west -- the only road that's marked on the west is Siroki Brijeg. Is that the direction that you came from?

utterances.speaker: JADRANKO MARTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To you, and don't hold it against me, when we look at Mostar, west is also the direction of Citluk and Medjugorje and Siroki Brijeg, but I did come from the direction of Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to know because I was intrigued about the Ahmici mention. I'm sure it was a misinterpretation. Thank you very much. And we are much obliged to you for coming here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judges' questions? It seems not. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming here to give your evidence. Sometimes we discuss some legal issues which have nothing to do with you so don't mind about that. We all wish you good luck in your future. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, and if I made any mistakes, it wasn't deliberate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as the witness is being taken out and before our next witness comes here, could we go into private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even at the cost of cutting shorter my direct examination, I need to address the Court now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session. But before that, before that, I would like to know whether there is any document to tender through this witness? I understand that the street map of Mostar that is P11.18 was marked by the witness himself. I don't see there is any objections. So this document is admitted into the evidence. How about others? Mr. Scott do you have any other documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask if we could follow the more or less normal procedure that I would prepare a written submission of the documents that we used, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but don't be too late.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could -- well, maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you could get some more information about that document, we would like to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Yes. I think in light of that in particular, I'll have to make a submission in any event to the Chamber will allow me, please, I'll make one -- a single submission. I just thought I would make the comment just because of Judge Clark's concerns about Ahmici, I heard the same thing and it was in the transcript but when I came back to and asked the questions about where the family was and he said it was Split and I assumed the earlier statement must have been a mistake but thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to -- yes, we will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we go into the closed session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good day to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could the ELMO be lowered a little so that I can have eye contact with the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, I believe that after your question, you have to turn off your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, before we begin, I wish to inform you that the Chamber has approved protective measures which consist of the protection of your name, voice and image, so that it will not be possible to identify you, and those parts of our conversation which contain information according to which you might be identified, will be in closed session. During your testimony, please be careful not to mention your name or your nickname or anything by which you might be identified. Before we begin, please look at this piece of paper. It should contain your name. If that is your name, please say yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. I will try to speak slowly in order to make it easier for the interpreters. Please watch the red light on my microphone and when it is turned off, then you can begin answering. And I will indicate to you with my hand whether you should speak faster or slower.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: We will now proceed and for the first set of questions, I ask to go into private session because these are questions by which the witness might be identified?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: In our conversation, we shall start from the time when the conflict with the Serbs broke out, from the answers that you gave us so far, I understood this is where you were living with your whole family. Can you tell us briefly how did you and your family see that conflict between -- with the Serbs? Can you tell us what was your family characteristic of, how did you act at the time, what did you do? How did you manage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, during the war with the Serbs, I continued living where I've already pointed out, and I saw it like all my neighbours. To my mind it was an aggression, an aggression in which we had to organise ourselves, to defend ourselves, to protect our families, and the property we had acquired.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did anything special happen? Did -- were there any casualties? Did anything happen to any of your members of the family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, yes, the city was exposed to the shelling all the time and yes, there were casualties, there were casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I mean your family. How did you fare?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: As for the family that was with me, we were all unscathed except that my father was killed, but he did not live with me. He lived outside Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you mean he was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: He was simply shot dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: We are being warned that we are moving too fast for the interpreters. My apologies to the interpreters. I will slow down a little and I will also make you a sign to slow down. Very well. So during that period of time, we see what happened to you. At that time, did you know Vinko Martinovic, Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes, I did know him. The whole Martinovic family. I've known them for some 40 years before that and I was on very good terms with them. We were quite friendly. There was human understanding between us. And I knew Mr. Vinko personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So you say good, neighbourly relations between you're two families and Vinko, how is it that you know him? On what kind of terms were you with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, you see, since I knew them, since I knew Vinko's parents and Vinko, I knew him since he was a boy and I have a son who is more or less his peer and they were pals. So I know Vinko in this respect quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: At that time, during the conflict with the Serbs, did you have -- did you see Vinko during that conflict, do you know that he played a role during that conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did. I did, Vinko and all the others, all the other lads, boys, who wanted to defend, they organised in a manner of speaking, they got together, helped civilians and they simply organised themselves so as to be ready to defend.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You say they organised themselves. How were they organised, in some military formations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: No, just like that. It was early days. It looked -- I mean organisation was getting together, protection of property, protection of all that property that could be endangered by the aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I see. Very well. But these are very early days and at the time did you see Vinko Martinovic in uniform? Did he join some unit, some army or anything? Did he resist? Did you used to see him in an uniform during the war against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes, I did see Vinko Martinovic in a uniform and I think that he belonged to HOS units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What were those units, HOS units, at the time? What did they do, who did they bring together? Can you tell us something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, in my field of knowledge, those were units ready to defend, to simply defend themselves against the aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know if Vinko Martinovic had a position in HOS? Was he something more than a foot soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: No. I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know anything about how at that time, that is where against the Serbs, how did Vinko Martinovic treat Bosniaks, Muslims? What was his attitude to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, since we used to see one another, since we were practically next door neighbours, from what I know, Vinko's attitude was very correct with either their boys or those who were older than he was. He lived, thought, organised when necessary, something, I mean very correctly and to the satisfaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let us now get out of the war with the Serbs. Do you recall the day when the conflict between the Muslims and Croats broke out and do you know what date it was in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it. It was the 9th of May, 1991 -- sorry, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court now briefly what happened to your family that day? How did that day begin? When did you see that the conflict was starting? Tell us in your own words, tell us your experience of that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, when this conflict broke out, I was in my flat with my wife, my daughter, my son, and my grandchild. Early in the morning, it could have been 5.00 or 6.00. We could hear some strange noise, how to put it, some strange din from the area of the yard where my flat is. So it woke me up and I got up and my wife did, and we started wondering what it could have been and at first I thought, since the Serb aggression was already under way, that it was general mobilisation of all of us who were able-bodied, that that was the moment when all of us who felt responsible were supposed to go. And while I was thinking about it, somebody knocked on the door of my flat. So I went there, I said, "Hello." And two soldiers turned up there, decent, and all they said to me was, "Come down stairs, please." And I asked them, "What's this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. about? Is it mobilisation or what?" And they said, "come down stairs and you'll find out." And then I asked should any other members of the family come along? They said, "No, only you." So I got ready straight away and I went downstairs into the yard and I saw those two uniformed soldiers moving ahead of me, some 20 metres ahead of me. And one of them turned back and said to me, "You sir, go back to your flat." And I stopped, I was rather lost, but they went on and then I turned and went back to my flat and my wife asks me, "So what happened?" And I told her what I just told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. So that was the 9th of May, the morning and so on. And did anything else happen that day? Did you stay there in your flat? Did anybody come to disturb you again or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: That same day, we could hear, we could still hear how somebody was passing through the yard, some shouts, and a lot of noise, and looking through the window I could see groups of people going in different direction. Here and there I could see uniformed men moving next to them. That is one could feel some excitement, some commotion, a situation which was not normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were you -- did you then begin to fear for yourself? Did you know what was going on? Did you take some steps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Absolutely. I realised what it could be about, of course I was afraid and I thought about a great many things, about how to save our lives to avoid that the -- to avoid that my family be placed under threat, and to see that my life is not in danger. Naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So did you do anything in this regard to make yourself safer to get rid of that fear? Did you do anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, listen, I thought how and in what way could I do it? And since in the meantime I'd met Mr. Ivan, Vinko's father, I sort of timidly said, "Ivan, if Vinko could do something, if he is in a position to protect me, to my family somehow, to avoid something," and Ivan said, "Right, I'll try."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can we have the redaction? The witness has mentioned -- the witness has used his name so it needs to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So go slowly but just take care. This has been redacted. Nobody will hear that but let's see that your name or nickname does not appear. So without mentioning your name, go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: And as the days went by, this insecurity increased with every day because there were still those groups of people who went around flats, who took people away, who threatened peace. I did not have much opportunity to move around at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I think we somehow glossed over what Ivan Martinovic told you. Let's go back to that. You turned to him and asked for help. And what did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: He said, "Well I'll do my best. I'll tell Vinko what this is about." And I believe that Vinko will be able to do something for you."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you believe him? Did you think he was really being sincere or did -- or that he said that only to calm you down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, you know, I've known him for a long time so, yes, I placed my full trust in them and I expected and knowing Vinko himself, his determination, his readiness to protect me at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. So you stayed in that flat, the days went by, the situation as such as it is. Did anybody else tomorrow could your door? Did you have any -- did you suffer any other unpleasant moments or was it all -- were there any other problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, yes, during the next months or so, and it was around half past 9.00 in the evening, and my door bell was rung by individuals, so I opened the door and saw a soldier armed and a civilian with him, and they asked me to see my papers, and my family's papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Just a moment. So we understand. Who is in the flat? You opened the door. Who was in the flat with you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: When they came to my flat, my wife, my son, and my grandson were there next to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And how old was your son then?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Go on. So they wanted to see your papers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: I gave them my documentation. They looked at each other, said, "Who else lives here with you?" And I told them, my wife -- I, my wife, my son, daughter-in-law, and the grandson, and they asked, "Then where is your son?" My wife got scared at that moment. As a mother, she thought -- she simply said, "He's gone with Vinko." May I say his name? Yes. "He went with Vinko." And they sort of stopped and said, "Which Vinko?" And my mom said, "Vinko, Stela, Martinovic," and I felt that they looked at one another and a few seconds later, after thinking about it, they gave me my papers back and said, "Sorry," sort of, "We made a mistake."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. So they returned your documents. Did they then leave and you closed the door and went back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes, they left but they also said, "We'll be back."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And after that, did you do anything or did you merely wait to see what would happen next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, you know, after they said, "We'll be back," of course, it is night-time and all that so that I was in some kind of -- and I decided to go to a neighbour who lived next to me and who knew Mr. Vinko Martinovic to ask him to somehow go to his base to let him know, and this young woman went there, she didn't find Vinko, but she found his men there. In the meantime Vinko also returned, so Vinko did not come personally but he did send his men to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So your neighbour went there, she found Vinko, and he sent soldiers. Are you sure that it was he who sent those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes, because those soldiers are my acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And did they tell you that Vinko had sent them to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes. They said, "Vinko can't come right now but we could," so they stayed at our place for about one hour and interviewed because I could recognise those people how they were dressed and really did not know those men, so I could not tell them about that but they said, "There will be no problem. We shall let Vinko -- we shall report it to Vinko and we shall also pay you frequent visits so that you feel that we are helping you so that you feel more secure and" ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And was it like that all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, you know, as time went by I joined the civilian defence units and then I had the opportunity of meeting Mr. Vinko himself, and in short conversations, I could tell him in case, because Vinko was always very forthcoming and he talked with me and it meant a great deal to me at the time, because even a nice greeting was also a major prize, and he was always ready for that and yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell us about one of those conversations with Vinko? What does he ask you? How is it? How can we see that he's looking after you? Can you tell us about it in your words? Can you recount one of these conversations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, listen, when he asks you, "Well, how are you, any problems? How is your security? How did you live? Enough food? Because at that time it was critical even to get by some food or cigarettes and Vinko was always ready to either from his mother or from his folk to simply halve their ration and then bring to my family and give me a package or a carton of cigarettes. And that was major help at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes. I can understand that. So he helped you even where supplies were concerned, cigarettes and that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Tell this Court, in that situation, what did it mean to you? Did you feel different owing to that, differently than before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, you know, it meant a return to life because when you are helpless and then somebody turns up who guarantees -- well, not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. guarantees, but guarantees and approaches you in this way, that is something completely different. You start living again because that was a time of such depression and all that, I -- and many things, when you start thinking about them, are simply hopeless.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But tell us, please, how is that Vinko guaranteed? What was he that he could protect you, to help you feel safe? Where did you see that he could give you this security and make you believe it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, to begin with, Vinko was a soldier, a uniformed soldier. Secondly, I know his determination, and his readiness because I know him, that he is even ready to physically oppose somebody at a given moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So this was his -- how he treated you and your family. Do you know perhaps, how he treated other Bosniaks, other Muslims, at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: In the area in which I lived, there were many Muslims. I never heard from anyone of them, I mean from my nearest neighbours, that they held any grudge against Vinko, that they had any objections to Vinko's behaviour. They simply had no knowledge of any things that would be wrong with Vinko.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Well, and did you hear perhaps if somebody said how he'd been helped by him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: I've heard it, yes, I heard it from a number of people who say, thanks be to him. He has done it, just as I say, he did me a favour for my family, yes, there are such people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you hear -- did you ever see Vinko persecute anyone, a family, a Muslim family from the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: I used to see Vinko often in my area, but that I did not see. That I did not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you see his soldiers evicting somebody, persecuting? Did you see them doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: No, even though I know individual soldiers of his but, no, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How is it that you know his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, you know, they are also lads from the neighbourhood, just as I knew Vinko I knew a few of them because they were my son's peers and naturally they palled up and of course I knew them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, did you hear stories about how Vinko persecuted, Bosniaks, Muslims? Did you ever hear those stories?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Why, yes, I did, I heard them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And did you check those stories? Do you know if they are true or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, they were things when -- I mean, to my mind, they are not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What does it mean, "to your mind"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, I mean because I know, and I didn't see, and many neighbours say that Vinko did not do it, that is that their not true, then I have no reason to say that that was so when it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And did you perhaps hear those stories saying how various criminal groups impersonated his men, how they said that they had his orders? Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it, I heard from some neighbours. I also think that there were such groups who, on behalf or rather in the name of Mr. Vinko, who misrepresented themselves, yes, my nearest neighbours said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: At that time, therefore, so you enjoyed some protection, and you're living here and time goes by and as far as I understand, you joined the civil defence. Now, what is it? What kind of duties did you perform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, the duty of the civil defence was the reception of the humanitarian aid, its storage and its distribution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you now tell us how was this humanitarian relief distributed? Was any distinction drawn between Croats, Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: When the war broke out between -- with Serbs, every family was given its personal card, noting down -- recording the number of members of the family, and that is -- and on the basis of these cards, people received packages, and there was no distinction. All of us, Croats and Muslims and Serbs, received those packages, all of us who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And that civil defence, did Ivan Martinovic -- was in the civil defence with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Yes, we were together from the beginning to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How did he behave? How did he treat Muslims that -- you were in daily contact? Was there some difference as against the period before the war with Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Well, listen in those units, there were Serbs and Muslims and Croats. Mr. -- may I mention his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Mr. Ivan very correctly with great dignity, and very humanely treated everybody equally. I never noticed that somebody enjoyed more rights or more privileges than I did or more access to him or somebody. To him, everybody was equal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Tell me, we are coming to the end of my examination, I only have a few more questions left, could you tell us what your situation is now as a Muslim in that part of Mostar? Do you still feel insecure? Do you suffer any other sort of pressure because you're a Muslim living in that mainly Croatian neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: As regards physical insecurity, I have no problems with that. My only insecurity is financial insecurity. I am unemployed. There are four of us in the family. And that's my only problem. And that is the biggest source of anxiety for my family and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Your other neighbours, Croats, do they have the same problems or do you have these problems because you're a Muslim? How do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: There are such problems but perhaps to a lesser extent. When the conflict broke out, Muslims lost their jobs, and now because the economy has been destroyed, it's very hard. Some people remained there but there is no discrimination. There are others -- I mean them, who are in the same position as me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, I have no further questions for you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, cross-examination, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good evening, Witness MB. My name is Roland Bos for the Prosecution and I will ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MB
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness MB, let me start by asking, you've said that there were other Muslims in the neighbourhood where you lived who said that they were also protected by Mr. Martinovic. Could you give me, please, the names of these persons and if necessary we can go into private session. We will go into private session, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'm moving to another topic. I can try to do it in four minutes but it may exceed so maybe this is a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also suggest that we break now and that I use the four minutes to tell you about the witnesses we have planned for tomorrow, and also to tender some documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, would you please show the witness out of the room after you pull down the blinds? Well, Witness, during your stay in The Hague, please do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You are still under the oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: See you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are trying to adhere to the order we gave you, so that tomorrow we envisage the continuation of this testimony. That's witness number 3. Then we intend to call and possibly complete witness number 4. If there is time left, we shall bring in witness 6 and not witness 5. That is our plan. If we can complete all this tomorrow, there will be one witness left for Monday. And that would be witness number 5. We have another group of witnesses arriving on Sunday and these are the four witnesses -- I can provide their names if our learned friends do not already have them. And we hope that we will be able to continue calling the witnesses in the order we announced. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for your information. I'm so glad that we pick up some speed for those witnesses. As for -- we have many witnesses who testified almost the same thing. So I believe that we could speed up a little bit. But unfortunately, this week, we could not finish all five witnesses. At most, we will finish four witnesses tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We plan to continue examining these witnesses in the same way as this witness. The same goes for the next group of witnesses. So the time will be roughly the same for each witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. How about the documents you are going to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no documents with these groups of witnesses. We will not tender any documents except perhaps maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. So I think we have to rise until tomorrow afternoon in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 7.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of July, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
